themes.summary: Customers appreciate the pricing as competitive and often cheaper than Audible, with some noting savings and good value despite slightly higher per-credit costs. Free trial and free credit opportunities are mentioned positively and negatively.
themes.action: Audit free trial and credit redemption flows to ensure cancellation and billing processes are transparent and prevent unintended charges; highlight pricing advantage in onboarding.

themes.summary: Customers appreciate easy navigation in general, but several report that search is vague or difficult to use for finding specific titles, genres, or book sections. Some request chapter-level navigation instead of track-based grouping.
themes.action: Improve search filtering and auto-complete; add chapter-level navigation option; add tagging/troupe filtering for genre discovery.

themes.summary: Customers consistently praise the wide variety and good selection of audiobooks available, including both classic and new titles. Some note limitations in library range, missing titles from specific authors, or restricted availability for certain books.
themes.action: Audit the catalog for gaps in popular authors and series; establish partnerships or licensing agreements to expand availability in high-demand segments.

themes.summary: Customers appreciate features like adjustable playback speed, sleep timer, and the ability to skip chapters or rewind a few seconds upon resuming. Some wish for progress percentage display or easier chapter navigation.
themes.action: Add a visual progress bar showing percentage of book completion; ensure chapter navigation is easily accessible from playback screen.

themes.summary: Customers frequently praise the app for being easy to use, straightforward, and helpful for their audiobook listening needs. Some express concern about overall functionality, complexity, or feel the app is rudimentary compared to alternatives.
themes.action: Conduct a detailed UX audit comparing the app interface to Audible and similar competitors, focusing on reducing perceived 'clunkiness' and adding polish to core navigation flows.

themes.summary: One customer reports significant friction with the bookmark system, noting lag and the need to manually delete dozens of bookmarks when revisiting a book, and questions whether bookmarks are stored locally or in the cloud.
themes.action: Implement a 'delete all bookmarks' feature and optimize bookmark storage and retrieval performance; document bookmark storage architecture for user clarity.

themes.summary: Customers value the ability to connect to CarPlay and car speakers, though some experience inconsistent Bluetooth connections and note that playback speed cannot be adjusted from the car interface.
themes.action: Debug Bluetooth/CarPlay connection reliability; enable playback speed adjustment from car interface; test with major car models.

themes.summary: Customers praise audio quality and voice narration as clear and easy to understand. No significant complaints about audio are reported.
themes.action: Continue to monitor audio quality standards and consider highlighting narration quality in marketing materials.

themes.summary: Multiple customers report that syncing between web and phone versions is unreliable or 'wonky,' creating friction when switching between devices.
themes.action: Audit and fix sync architecture between web and mobile apps; add user-facing sync status indicators and error messages.

themes.summary: Customers mention the VIP section, with mixed feedback: some find it good, while others note that while it has a decent number of titles, few are personally relevant to them.
themes.action: Review VIP tier curation and personalization; consider adding preference-based recommendations to increase relevance.

themes.summary: Customers note that the interface is generally easy to use but could be more polished or intuitive. Some request a visual bookshelf feature or clearer icon meanings.
themes.action: Conduct a design audit of icon clarity and labeling; consider adding an optional visual bookshelf library view; benchmark UI against Audible and Libby.

caveats: Sentences from the same verbatim are not independent observations; clustering inflates apparent significance.
Themes can overlap (a verbatim may belong to several), so groups aren't mutually exclusive as most tests assume.
Sentiment scores are LLM judgments, not a validated instrument; treat them as a consistent proxy, not ground truth.
Source data is a convenience sample (whoever chose to post), not a random sample of customers.
Only 37 sentences — confidence intervals will be wide and rankings unstable between runs.
11 themes tested; Bonferroni correction applied, which is conservative and may hide real effects.
